source_notes.label: Precursor chemistry and distinct synthesis controls
source_notes.summary: Aminoarsine is conditioned with oleylamine at 40 °C until bubbling stops, consistent with source-proposed transamination. Exact reacted molecular species is unknown. The quantified 1 mmol cyanoborohydride recipe gives pure InAs; the 0.5 mmol and 3/6 mmol comparisons are distinct incompletely specified observations. Excess reductant promotes metallic In, while NaCl is a washing-dependent by-product.
source_locators: Supporting Information PDF p. 3,13, Sections 1.2.1–1.2.2, 2.1 and Figure S2

source_notes.label: Washing comparison does not overwrite the reported recipe
source_notes.summary: The typical recipe explicitly uses a first toluene/methanol/isopropanol wash and two later toluene/ethanol washes, each centrifuged at 4500 rpm for 10 min. Figure S2b compares ethanol versus methanol purification and reports NaCl removal using methanol. Complete alternative volumes and sequence are not supplied, so the observation is preserved separately.
source_locators: Supporting Information PDF p. 4,13, Workup and Figure S2b

source_notes.label: Parent QDs and ligand-exchanged QDs are separate samples
source_notes.summary: Pristine oleylamine-capped InAs has a reported 2.2 nm TEM mean and In/As ratio 1.04. After exchange, the source reports retained phase, morphology and absorption, decreased interparticle distance, loss of N 1s, S 2p near 163 eV and In/As 1.13. It does not report a newly measured 2.2 nm mean for the exchanged sample.
source_locators: Supporting Information PDF p. 14–15,26–27, Figures S3 and S12

source_notes.label: Surface chemistry is not bulk phase purity
source_notes.summary: Pristine XRD is consistent with zinc-blende InAs, while XPS shows about 3 at% surface oxygen and a weak As(III)-consistent contribution. A phase-pure diffraction pattern does not establish an oxygen-free surface. The ICSD patterns are references, not refined specimen atomic coordinates.
source_locators: Supporting Information PDF p. 14–15, Section 2.2 and Figure S3

source_notes.label: Electrode fabrication and flooding are source-specific contexts
source_notes.summary: Native oleylamine-capped QDs are deposited from toluene with a later Nafion layer for H-cell tests. Exchanged QDs are deposited from ethanol with a mixed binder ink for flow-cell tests. Source observations associate residual oleylamine with loss of support hydrophobicity; the mechanism is proposed, and no contact angle is measured or inferred from the droplet photograph.
source_locators: Supporting Information PDF p. 5–6,25–26, Electrode crafting and Figure S11

source_notes.label: Catalytic metrics belong to the electrode and testing regime
source_notes.summary: Near-unity formate Faradaic efficiency is the flow-cell result for exchanged-QD electrodes in 1 M KOH. The native-ligand H-cell in 1 M KHCO3 peaks near 55% at −5 mA/cm2. These are not properties of an isolated pristine particle or claims of complete electrochemical parameter coverage. Main-figure captions retain one-hour chronopotentiometry and their controls.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–4, Figures 1–3 and catalytic discussion

source_notes.label: Reconstruction and active phase are distinct kinds of evidence
source_notes.summary: Post-electrolysis STEM/EDS indicates In-rich agglomerates and partially oxidized InAs1−x; ex-situ XPS is In-rich and As-depleted with predominantly In2O3. Metallic indium as the operative active phase is the authors’ interpretation of electrochemistry, not the same claim as the ex-situ oxide signal. Detailed SI post-electrolysis specimen comparisons are outside the selected pages.
